predictions.selection_reason: user-controlled startTag and endTag directly interpolated into git diff command -> executed via shell -> potential command injection
predictions.source_summary: startTag and endTag are parameters passed to the gitDiffApply function (lines 36-37). They are user-provided inputs to the module with no evidence of validation or sanitization.
predictions.sink_summary: The utils.run function uses child_process.exec (line 10 of src/run.js) which executes commands in a shell, allowing shell metacharacters and command injection if untrusted input is interpolated.
predictions.guard_summary: No validation, sanitization, or escaping of startTag/endTag before interpolation into shell command. The only check is equality comparison (line 220: startTag === endTag) and non-empty check. The checkOutTag function also interpolates tags into git commands without sanitization.
predictions.risk_pattern: User-controlled parameters startTag and endTag are directly interpolated into a shell command string that is executed via child_process.exec, enabling command injection if tags contain shell metacharacters.
enclosing_conditions: Only if patchFile content is non-empty (line 136)
predictions.context_summary: The createPatchFile function generates a git diff patch between two tags. It's part of a git diff/apply utility that clones repositories, checks out tags, and applies differences. The tags are used in multiple shell commands throughout the codebase without sanitization.
unresolved_facts: Whether the calling code validates/sanitizes tags before passing to gitDiffApply
Whether tags are expected to come from trusted sources only
Whether there are any external security controls not visible in the repository
